content: Before taking cefuroxime, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, penicillins, other cephalosporin antibiotics (such as cephalexin), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other complications. This medication may cause dizziness or drowsiness, which can be exacerbated by alcohol or marijuana (cannabis). Limit your consumption of alcoholic beverages. Cefuroxime may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used if clearly necessary, as it passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Always keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as diabetic urine tests or blood glucose tests, potentially causing false results. If someone overdoses and experiences severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only and should not be used for other purposes unless directed by your doctor. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. If you experience side effects such as nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, stomach pain, dizziness, or drowsiness, contact your doctor. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile), which can occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may result in oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. If you experience any unusual symptoms, seek medical advice promptly.
